transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-09
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Mariner CTO), Ben Liu (Platform Eng), Carlos Mendes (Security)

Summary: integration discovery focused on SDK support (Python/Node), LangChain / LlamaIndex adapters, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for latency and data residency constraints.

[00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick intros — i'm ethan, AE on the infra team, and with me is sofia, our solutions engineer. how are you all doing?
[00:08] Aisha (Mariner CTO): doing well, thanks. big day, excited to dig in.
[00:12] Ben (Mariner Platform Eng): yep, thanks. we want to understand integration surface and operational controls.
[00:18] Sofia (Redwood SE): great. goal for today: map your current stack, talk SDKs/langchain/llamaindex support, gateway/proxy patterns, quotas, and what observability looks like—then outline next steps. sound good?
[00:29] Carlos (Mariner Security): yep, and we need to validate SOC2/HSM/KMS stuff too.

[02:00] Ethan: quick qual — what's your target latency SLAs and typical throughput? any peak windows?
[02:10] Ben: right now most calls are synchronous user-facing chat — target p95 around 400-600ms per token generation is ideal. peaks during product launch can hit ~250 rps for short bursts, but sustained is more like 50-100 rps.
[02:30] Sofia: got it. are you using any existing LLM provider in prod?
[02:36] Aisha: we've piloted openai for internal features, but costs and data residency are big concerns. looking at hosted first but dedicated or private for regulated customers.

[04:00] Ethan: makes sense. on the SDK side we have official python and node SDKs, and we provide connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. sofia, do you want to call out the libs?
[04:12] Sofia: yeah — we ship a Redwood SDK with the familiar client.generate/chat/embeddings methods. for LangChain we provide a RedwoodLLM wrapper and an embeddings adapter — community patterns are supported; same for LlamaIndex via our index adapter. we also publish examples for each. docs live at redwood.ai/docs/sdk (note: link shared in chat).
[04:45] Ben: how seamless is the switch? if we have existing LangChain pipelines, what's the migration effort?
[04:52] Sofia: typically small: swap the provider class import, update auth (api key or mTLS for private), and adjust any model names. we also have a middleware for retry/backoff to map Redwood errors to langchain-friendly exceptions.

[06:10] Carlos: what about network patterns? we have a central API gateway and would prefer to keep calls internal — any proxy or gateway recommendations?
[06:18] Ethan: customers commonly run a sidecar/gateway pattern. for hosted they hit Redwood public endpoints through your gateway/proxy; for dedicated you can set up private peering or VPC endpoints; for private on-prem we deploy a local runtime behind your gateway. sofia: any notes on rate limiting?
[06:40] Sofia: we expose rate limit headers and quota controls at the API key and org level. you can configure per-route quotas and burst limits. when integrating with your gateway it's common to enforce an additional layer to smooth spikes. we also recommend using prefix caching for large context reuse to reduce token spend and improve latency.

[08:05] Ben: prefix caching — can we control TTL and eviction? and is KV cache exposed?
[08:14] Sofia: yes — caching is configurable. our KV cache for session/state can be kept on the runtime with configurable TTLs. for Dedicated/Private you can point it to your Redis or our managed cache; eviction policies are exposed via config. there may be slight differences in behavior across quantized runtimes but APIs are consistent.

[10:00] Aisha: security: we need KMS key control and audit logs. where does key management live?
[10:08] Ethan: for hosted we integrate with a customer-managed KMS for enterprise plans (bring-your-own-key). Dedicated gives you isolated hardware pools and can use your KMS/ HSM. Private deployments run in your network and use your KMS/HSM directly. we stream audit logs to your SIEM and keep request traces for N days based on retention policy.
[10:35] Carlos: what's the retention window and can we restrict staff access?
[10:40] Sofia: retention is configurable; default for enterprise is 90 days, but can be extended. RBAC and SSO (SAML/OIDC) integrate with your IdP, and we also offer granular token-level permissions.

[12:00] Speaker 1: question — model versioning and rollouts?
[12:06] Sofia: model pinning and rollouts are first-class: you can pin endpoints to model versions, create canary splits, and auto-fallback to smaller/compatible variants on errors. metric-based rollouts (latency/cost or accuracy) are supported in the console.

[14:00] Ben: curious about telemetry. We use Datadog and Prometheus. how do observability hooks look?
[14:08] Sofia: we emit metrics via Prometheus-compatible endpoints for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we push to Datadog via an integration or you can pull logs via our webhook. We also provide per-request tracing IDs that tie into your distributed trace so you can correlate app->inference latency. there are token-level cost breakdowns in the Console.

[16:00] Aisha: latency — you mentioned kernel selection and hardware routing earlier. how much variance should we expect?
[16:10] Ethan: the runtime chooses kernels and scheduling based on model and request shape. hosted p95 numbers depend on model/sequence length; for smaller context we see very low latencies on optimized kernels. Dedicated gives more predictable percentiles because capacity is reserved. Private is as consistent as your infra. we can run benchmarks with your prompts to give a realistic picture.

[18:20] Ben: about embedding vectors — how do we handle vector datastore integrations? we use Pinecone and an internal vector DB for certain flows.
[18:30] Sofia: we output embeddings in standard float32 or quantized formats; we have quickstart examples for Pinecone, Milvus, and FAISS. embeddings calls can be batched and you can control concurrency/throughput limits.

[20:00] Carlos: compliance review — do you have SOC2 + ISO docs? any pen test reports?
[20:08] Ethan: yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation documents and a redacted pentest summary. for Private deployments we support air-gapped installs; for Dedicated we offer network isolation and contractually agreed SLAs.

[22:00] Aisha: cost is huge. can you walk through cost levers — batching, quantization, caching?
[22:08] Sofia: absolutely. batching improves throughput and lowers per-token cost but may add a bit of latency — we have dynamic batching with latency SLOs. quantization reduces memory and compute — great for Dedicated/Private. caching (prefix/KV) often gives the biggest bang for chat apps with repeated prompts. routing policies let you fall back to a cheaper variant when cost matters. we'll include a sample TCO sheet with rough numbers for your traffic profile.

[25:00] Ben: POC — we'd like to run a small POC: integrate with our LangChain pipelines, run 1k requests/day and benchmark latency and cost.
[25:09] Ethan: solid. typical POC steps: 1) share infra diagram and traffic sample; 2) Redwood provides access (hosted API key or Dedicated trial) + POC runbook; 3) run benchmarks with your prompts; 4) review metrics and decide next phase.

[27:00] Aisha: timeline — if we like results, target pilot in 6-8 weeks. procurement cycles probable for dedicated.
[27:10] Ethan: makes sense. we'll aim to accelerate with pre-filled contracts and a JIT security review.

[29:00] Speaker 2 (visitor): small question about rate limit headers — do you provide granular per-route headers?
[29:08] Sofia: yes, headers include X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset. We can also surface per-key usage breakdown in the Console and alert on anomalies via webhooks.

[31:00] Ben: any gotchas with LangChain streaming/chat integration? we rely on streaming tokens to the client.
[31:08] Sofia: we support server-sent events (SSE) and chunked responses, and our LangChain wrapper supports streaming. caveat: some proxies/gateways buffer chunked responses — you'll want to ensure your gateway passes them through or use web socket/proxy config to avoid buffering.

[33:30] Carlos: for dedicated, what connectivity options? vpn, private link, peering?
[33:38] Ethan: we support AWS PrivateLink, VPC peering, and site-to-site VPN. for multi-cloud we do region-local endpoints and can route by latency. Private on-prem is also possible but takes longer to provision.

[35:00] Aisha: ok, can you share a sample integration with our SDK + LangChain example?
[35:08] Sofia: yes — i'll drop a repo link in the follow-up with python/node examples, langchain wrapper, and a LlamaIndex adapter.

[37:00] Ben: SLA questions — what uptime and latency SLAs do you offer on Dedicated?
[37:06] Ethan: Dedicated comes with an SLA for uptime (four 9s for control plane, runtime depends on config) and latency SLOs depending on GPU family and reserved capacity. We'll include the SLA doc in the follow-up.

[39:10] Speaker 1: curious about fallback policies when a model is OOM or degraded.
[39:18] Sofia: we have automatic fallback to smaller model variants and a pre-warm cache policy. also circuit breakers at the routing layer so upstream services remain available.

[41:00] Aisha: procurement — when do we expect a quote and contract?
[41:08] Ethan: i'll send an initial hosted vs dedicated TCO and a ballpark quote by Friday (2027-02-11). if you want dedicated, procurement review will take longer — we'll loop legal early.

[43:00] Ben: any integrations for tracing — open telemetry?
[43:05] Sofia: we use OpenTelemetry for traces; you can export traces to your collector. we also provide trace IDs in API responses to correlate with your logs.

[45:00] Carlos: final security ask — can we run a short architecture review with your security team?
[45:08] Ethan: absolutely. i'll coordinate a 30-45 minute security deep dive next week with our security engineer.

[47:00] Ethan: recap of next steps: we'll send pricing/TCO, SOC2/ISO docs, SDK/langchain examples, and propose POC dates. sofia will prepare POC runbook. ben will share infra diagram and sample traffic. any other items?
[47:20] Aisha: that covers it, thanks.
[47:25] Ben: thanks, appreciate it.
[47:30] Sofia: thanks everyone, we'll follow up.

End of transcript.
